environment: Local worktree via Tailscale, browser UI only for creation and edits
stop_early: All four quality dimensions at least 4/5, no major missing purpose or broken rendering

scoring.purpose: 1 misses the idea; 3 mostly conveys it with important gaps; 5 communicates the central idea and appropriate response fully
scoring.clarity: 1 confusing or inaccessible; 3 understandable with rough or insider language; 5 concise, welcoming and clear for a curious newcomer
scoring.flow: 1 dead ends or contradictory structure; 3 usable but thin choices or weak follow-up; 5 coherent progression, meaningful response options and next steps
scoring.visual: 1 broken or unreadable; 3 usable with crowding or weak imagery; 5 readable, consistent, relevant imagery and accessible scrolling
scoring.edit_fidelity: Per edit: 0 ignored/failed, 0.5 partly fulfilled, 1 fulfilled; record collateral changes separately

limitations: No code/model changes during the twelve runs
Preview buttons intentionally cannot be clicked; navigation structure assessed from visible cards and plans, not live viewer playback
Seed library-video and email-delivery features may be approximated with supported content
Subjective agent assessment, not human user research or independent historical/theological fact-checking

targets.title: Fact or Fiction
targets.prompt: Make a short Fact or Fiction journey for someone curious or sceptical about Jesus. Help them think about whether the story of Jesus can be trusted, give them a little historical context, and finish by asking who they think Jesus was. Keep it welcoming and let them express what they actually think.
essentials: some concrete historical context without overstating evidence
space for sceptical as well as positive responses

targets.title: What About the Resurrection?
targets.prompt: Create a short journey called What About the Resurrection? for someone exploring Christianity. Invite them to think about the empty tomb and the different explanations for it, explain why Christians believe Jesus really died and rose again, and ask what that would mean for how they see Christianity. Make room for doubt rather than assuming they already believe.
essentials: Jesus really died, Christian claim of resurrection
support or evidence with honest framing
personal implications and room for uncertainty

targets.title: What's Jesus Got to Do With Me?
targets.prompt: Make a short journey about what Jesus' death and resurrection have to do with me personally. It's for someone who isn't sure they are good enough for God. Help them explore grace, Jesus' love and forgiveness, and give them a chance to say what they think or what they are unsure about. Keep it down to earth and not preachy.
essentials: grace rather than earning God's acceptance
love, forgiveness and freedom from sin

targets.title: Decision / Can I Know Him?
targets.prompt: Create a gentle journey for someone deciding whether to follow Jesus. Explain that Jesus wants a relationship with them, let them respond yes, not yet, or unsure, and give each response a helpful next step. For someone who says yes, help them express a simple prayer of trust and suggest how to begin growing in faith. Don't pressure people who aren't ready.
essentials: distinct yes/not yet/unsure responses with suitable next steps
prayer includes thanks/love, forgiveness/turning, trust/new life
